introduction_paragraph: Emotion recognition is fundamental for understanding human behavior and enhancing human-computer interaction. However, achieving accurate emotion detection across diverse real-world scenarios remains challenging when emotions are expressed through multiple modalities—facial expressions, vocal tones, and linguistic content. Traditional single-modality approaches often fail to capture the full complexity of human emotional expression. To address this, we developed a Multi-Architecture Late Fusion system combining BERT, Wav2Vec2, and MIMAMO Net for empathetic emotion recognition. Our system processes 24,696 conversational samples across 7 emotion classes from a dataset of 14,817 training conversations. The Combined Fusion model achieves 84.83% accuracy by integrating audio-text (84.21%) and video models (53.09%) with learned fusion weights (31.4% video, 68.6% audio-text), demonstrating that intelligent multimodal fusion significantly outperforms single-modality approaches in naturalistic conversational contexts.
